title: Finite-stage rational and Karoubi coherence of completed exchange
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and the finite intermediate coefficient fields of [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Let $f:X\to S$, $g:T\to S$, $h:Y\to X$, $e:Y\to T$ form a Cartesian square [sbc-def-base-change-square]. Assume all four schemes are noetherian and finite-dimensional and $\ell$ is invertible on $S$. No smoothness or constructible landing hypothesis is imposed. For each field $E$ and corner $W$, put $\mathcal B_E(W)=D_{\mathrm{comp}}(W,\mathcal O_E)$, $\mathcal R_E(W)=\mathcal B_E(W)[1/\varpi_E]$, and $\mathcal C_E(W)=\Kar(\mathcal R_E(W))$, with the completed coefficient sheaves, raw scalar localizations and Karoubi conventions of [def-sbc-ambient-complete-coefficient-categories]. Use the actual integral completed operations $P_E^u=Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp},\mathcal O_E}$, $D_E^u=Ru_{*,\mathcal O_E}$ and their canonical natural exchange $\alpha_E^{\mathrm{int}}$ of [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange]. Write $C_W=C_{M/E,W}$ for the actual integral coefficient tensor of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

There are canonically specified additive raw rational and finite-stage Karoubi extensions of these operations and exchange, whose action for an integral linear functor $H$ is
$$H^{\mathrm{rat}}(u\otimes c)=H(u)\otimes c,\qquad H^{\mathrm{Kar}}(K,p)=(HK,H^{\mathrm{rat}}(p)).$$
A localized comparison $b:H\xrightarrow{\sim}J$ extends at $(K,p)$ with arrow $J(p)b_KH(p)$ and inverse $H(p)b_K^{-1}J(p)$. The raw exchange extends to the transformation with component $G_E(p)\alpha_E^{\mathrm{raw}}(K)F_E(p)$, where
$$F_E=P_E^fD_E^g,\qquad G_E=D_E^hP_E^e$$
now denote the extended functors $\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal C_E(X)$; the same notation with superscript $\mathrm{raw}$ denotes their raw versions. Its value on $j_EK=(K,1)$ is exactly $j_E(\alpha_E^{\mathrm{raw}}(K))$, for the canonical identity-idempotent inclusion $j_E$.

More precisely, let the canonical integral scalar comparisons be
$$p^u:C_UP_E^u\xrightarrow{\sim}P_M^uC_V,\qquad d^u:C_VD_E^u\xrightarrow{\sim}D_M^uC_U\quad(u:U\to V).$$
Their integral composites $(P_M^f d^g)\circ(p^fD_E^g)$ and $(D_M^h p^e)\circ(d^hP_E^e)$ extend to comparisons
$$b^F_{M/E}:T^X_{M/E}F_E\xrightarrow{\sim}F_MT^T_{M/E},\qquad b^G_{M/E}:T^X_{M/E}G_E\xrightarrow{\sim}G_MT^T_{M/E}.$$
The individual operation comparisons and these composite comparisons satisfy the unit and tower equations for the scalar associators in [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent], with identity coefficient transitions normalized as in [def-sbc-ambient-complete-coefficient-categories]. The extended canonical exchange satisfies, for every $K\in\mathcal C_E(T)$,
$$\alpha_M(T^T_{M/E}K)b^F_{M/E,K}=b^G_{M/E,K}T^X_{M/E}(\alpha_E(K)).$$
All these assertions also hold before the finite-stage Karoubi extension, on $\mathcal R_E$. The comparisons are the extensions of the specified integral scalar maps, including their tensor-unit normalizations at $M=E$; they are not arbitrary comparison isomorphisms. No invertibility of the exchange itself is asserted.

proof.text: On each integral category $\mathcal B_E(W)$, [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange] supplies the actual additive $\mathcal O_E$-linear functors $P_E^u,D_E^u$ and the natural transformation $\alpha_E^{\mathrm{int}}:P_E^fD_E^g\Rightarrow D_E^hP_E^e$. Its statement supplies naturality on every integral arrow, and identifies this transformation with the completed canonical mate. Thus the integral input here is defined on all derived-complete objects; neither a constructible restriction nor invertibility of the exchange is needed.

source.place: Lines 1218-1228: integral linear operations and their ambient extensions; specified integral mate

proof.text: For fixed $E$, apply the additive/semilinear part of [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] to each operation, taking $R=S=\mathcal O_E$, $t=u=\varpi_E$ and the identity coefficient homomorphism. By [lem-weil-l-adic-integers-localization-uniformizer], the localized coefficient ring is $E$, so its formula is $H^{\mathrm{raw}}(v\otimes c)=H(v)\otimes c$. Apply its natural-transformation clause to $\alpha_E^{\mathrm{int}}$. The resulting component is $\alpha_E^{\mathrm{int}}(K)\otimes1$, natural for every raw arrow. Its composition clause identifies the two extended composites with $F_E^{\mathrm{raw}}$ and $G_E^{\mathrm{raw}}$.

source.place: Lines 1193-1194 and 1218-1228: central localization of integral operations and exchange

proof.text:
By [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], for each $E\subset M$ the actual tensor functors $C_{M/E,W}$ preserve ambient completeness and carry the specified natural isomorphisms $p^u,d^u$. That statement gives their compatibility with successive coefficient extensions and identities. Write $H_E:\mathcal B_E(A)\to\mathcal B_E(B)$ for either an individual operation and $b^H_{M/E}:C^B_{M/E}H_E\to H_MC^A_{M/E}$ for its specified comparison. With integral tensor associators $a^A,a^B$, this successive-extension compatibility reads
$$b^H_{P/E}(a^B_{P,M,E}H_E)=(H_Pa^A_{P,M,E})(b^H_{P/M}C^A_{M/E})(C^B_{P/M}b^H_{M/E}).$$
Use the tensor-unit maps to identify $C_{E/E}$ with the identity, as required by [def-sbc-ambient-complete-coefficient-categories]; the identity comparison becomes $1_{H_E}$. The tower equation remains this equation under those identifications, by substitution of the tensor-unit isomorphisms on both sides. These are the specified tensor comparisons, rather than a new choice of isomorphisms.

source.place: Lines 1297-1321: actual integral tensor, tensor-unit normalization and associators

proof.text: For $E\subset M$, integral tensor $C_{M/E,W}$ is semilinear for $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_M$: tensoring $av$ gives the same arrow as multiplication by the image of $a$ on the tensor, by the balancing relation. The image of $\varpi_E$ is nonzero in the field $M$ and hence invertible; [lem-weil-l-adic-integers-localization-uniformizer] identifies $\mathcal O_M[1/\varpi_M]$ with $M$. Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] to $C$, and to the composite functors at the two ends of $p^u,d^u$. This gives exactly the raw scalar transition of [def-sbc-ambient-complete-coefficient-categories], $v\otimes c\mapsto C(v)\otimes c$ for $c\in E\subset M$. The same lemma localizes $p^u,d^u$, their inverses, the tensor associators, the unit equations and the operation tower equations of step 3; its preservation of whiskering and composition ensures these are equations with the actual extended operations.

source.place: Lines 1300-1321: localization between different coefficient rings and normalized coherent comparisons

proof.text:
Compose the raw operation comparisons to define
$$b^F=(P_M^f d^g)(p^fD_E^g),\qquad b^G=(D_M^h p^e)(d^hP_E^e).$$
These are the raw extensions of the integral composites, by step 4. The final clause of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] concerns the exchange $\gamma\circ\Lambda_X(b_K)$ for complete $K$: here $b_K:Lf^*Rg_*K\to Rh_*Le^*K$ is the ambient mate of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], $\Lambda$ is derived completion with unit $\kappa$, and $\gamma:\Lambda_XRh_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*\Lambda_Y$ is the arrow of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pushforward-completion], so $\gamma\kappa=Rh_*(\kappa)$. We identify it with $\alpha^{\mathrm{int}}_E$. By [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] $P_u=\Lambda Lu^*$ with completion unit $k_u$, hence $(\gamma\Lambda_X(b_K))k_{f,D_gK}=\gamma\kappa b_K=R_h(k_{e,K})b_K$. The canonical composition isomorphisms of step 1 are the conjugates of direct-image composition for $P_u\dashv D_u$; [lem-sbc-reflected-compositor-unit-normalization] gives $c^ck\,L(k)=k\,c$ for each of the two compositors, and composing these identities gives $\theta^c_Mk_{h,P_fM}L_h(k_{f,M})=k_{e,P_gM}L_e(k_{g,M})\theta_M$. Thus [lem-sbc-reflector-square-mate-factorization] applies, and its uniqueness clause gives $\alpha^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,K}=\gamma\Lambda_X(b_K)$; likewise at $M$. Step 2 then identifies the rationalizations. With the square labeled $(f,g,h,e)$, the clause is exactly
$$\alpha_M^{\mathrm{raw}}(T^T_{M/E}K)b^{F,\mathrm{raw}}_{M/E,K}=b^{G,\mathrm{raw}}_{M/E,K}T^X_{M/E}(\alpha_E^{\mathrm{raw}}(K)).$$
All four schemes satisfy that node's noetherian, finite-dimensional and invertible-$\ell$ hypotheses. Its ambient clause applies without assuming constructible landing.

source.place: Lines 1218-1228 and 1297-1321: the canonical rationalized exchange and coefficient comparisons

proof.text: Here is the finite-stage Karoubi functor calculation, using [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]. For an additive raw functor $H$, set $\widehat H(K,p)=(HK,H(p))$ and $\widehat H(v)=H(v)$. We suppress the superscript raw in the next calculations. Since $H(p)^2=H(p^2)=H(p)$ and $v=qvp$ implies $H(v)=H(q)H(v)H(p)$, these are valid objects and arrows. The identity at $(K,p)$ maps to $H(p)$, the required target identity, and $H(wv)=H(w)H(v)$. Additivity on arrows is inherited from $H$. Apply this construction to the operations and the raw transitions. It is the transition construction fixed in [def-sbc-ambient-complete-coefficient-categories], and $\widehat{JH}=\widehat J\widehat H$ on objects and arrows.

source.place: Lines 1208-1216, 1218-1228 and 1308-1312: extension on idempotent objects and supported arrows

proof.text:
For a raw natural transformation $\eta:H\Rightarrow J$, put $\widehat\eta_{(K,p)}=J(p)\eta_KH(p)$. It satisfies the support relation of [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]. Naturality for $p$ gives $J(p)\eta_K=\eta_KH(p)$, so this arrow is also $J(p)\eta_K=\eta_KH(p)$. For $v=qvp:(K,p)\to(L,q)$, we have $vp=v=qv$ and hence
$$J(v)\widehat\eta_{(K,p)}=J(v)\eta_K=\eta_LH(v)=\widehat\eta_{(L,q)}H(v).$$
This verifies naturality on every Karoubi arrow. In particular, $\eta=\alpha_E^{\mathrm{raw}}$ gives exactly $G_E(p)\alpha_E^{\mathrm{raw}}(K)F_E(p)$. At $p=1_K$ it is $\alpha_E^{\mathrm{raw}}(K)$, which is precisely the arrow $j_E(\alpha_E^{\mathrm{raw}}(K))$ between the identity-idempotent objects.

source.place: Lines 1208-1216 and 1218-1228: natural transformations restricted to idempotent summands

proof.text:
If $\eta=b:H\xrightarrow{\sim}J$, extend $b^{-1}$ by the same rule. The two supported composites are
$$[H(p)b_K^{-1}J(p)][J(p)b_KH(p)]=H(p),\qquad [J(p)b_KH(p)][H(p)b_K^{-1}J(p)]=J(p).$$
For the first equality use $J(p)b_K=b_KH(p)$, cancel $b_K^{-1}b_K$, and use $H(p)^2=H(p)$; the second uses $H(p)b_K^{-1}=b_K^{-1}J(p)$ and $J(p)^2=J(p)$. By [def-weil-karoubi-envelope] these are the identities of the corresponding Karoubi objects. Thus each localized comparison has the asserted component and inverse. This applies to $p^u,d^u,a$ and their composites.

source.place: Lines 1208-1216 and 1313-1321: comparison isomorphisms on summands

proof.text:
For completeness, the supported formulas preserve the operations forming the coherence equations. At $(K,p)$, the extended identity transformation is $H(p)$, the identity prescribed by [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]. For $\eta:H\Rightarrow J$ and $\zeta:J\Rightarrow L$, naturality at $p$ gives
$$[L(p)\zeta_KJ(p)][J(p)\eta_KH(p)]=L(p)\zeta_K\eta_KH(p)=\widehat{\zeta\eta}_{(K,p)}.$$
Whiskering on the target by $A$ sends $J(p)\eta_KH(p)$ to $AJ(p)A(\eta_K)AH(p)$, exactly the extension of $A\eta$; whiskering on the source by $B$ evaluates the same formula at $(BK,B(p))$, exactly the extension of $\eta B$. Together with step 6's equality for composite functors, these formulas show, by induction on compositions and whiskerings, that each raw comparison equation remains the same equation after extension. Equal raw components yield equal supported arrows, since Karoubi arrows are underlying arrows with a support relation.

source.place: Lines 1208-1216 and 1313-1321: explicit preservation of the finite coherence expressions

proof.text:
The composite comparisons also satisfy the tower equation. Use notation $U,V,W$ for the raw scalar transitions at the source, middle and target of $H_E:A_E\to B_E$, $J_E:B_E\to D_E$. Write $b=b^H$, $c=b^J$, and $k_{M/E}=J_M(b_{M/E})(c_{M/E}H_E)$. This is $b^F$ for $(H,J)=(D^g,P^f)$ and $b^G$ for $(P^e,D^h)$. The prescribed tower equation is that of [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent]. Suppress object arguments and write juxtaposition for composition, retaining right whiskerings. Expanding the left side and substituting the individual tower equations from steps 3-4 gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
k_{P/E}(a^D J_EH_E)
&=J_P(b_{P/E})(c_{P/E}H_E)(a^DJ_EH_E)\\
&=J_P(b_{P/E}a^B H_E)(c_{P/M}V_{M/E}H_E)(W_{P/M}c_{M/E}H_E)\\
&=J_PH_P(a^A)(J_Pb_{P/M}U_{M/E})(J_PV_{P/M}b_{M/E})
(c_{P/M}V_{M/E}H_E)(W_{P/M}c_{M/E}H_E).
\end{aligned}
$$
Naturality of $c_{P/M}$ at $b_{M/E,K}$ replaces the middle product by
$$(J_PV_{P/M}b_{M/E})(c_{P/M}V_{M/E}H_E)
=(c_{P/M}H_MU_{M/E})(W_{P/M}J_Mb_{M/E}).$$
The resulting expression is exactly
$$J_PH_P(a^A)(k_{P/M}U_{M/E})(W_{P/M}k_{M/E}),$$
the required tower right side. The unit comparison is $(J_E1)(1H_E)=1$. Step 9 now gives these equations on the Karoubi envelopes with the specified scalar associators of [def-sbc-ambient-complete-coefficient-categories].

source.place: Lines 1313-1321 and 1347-1359: tower compatibility for the composite operation families

proof.text:
Finally apply step 9 to the raw exchange equation of step 5. The extension of $\alpha_M^{\mathrm{raw}}T^T$ is $\alpha_MT^T$, the extensions of $b^F,b^G$ are their specified supported composites, and the extension of $T^X\alpha_E^{\mathrm{raw}}$ is $T^X\alpha_E$. Therefore its value at every $(K,p)$ is
$$\alpha_M(T^T_{M/E}(K,p))b^F_{M/E,(K,p)}=b^G_{M/E,(K,p)}T^X_{M/E}(\alpha_E(K,p)).$$
All components are the explicitly specified supported arrows in [def-sbc-ambient-complete-coefficient-categories]. Steps 4, 8 and 9 also preserve the individual operation unit and tower equations and the tensor-unit normalizations; step 10 handles the composites. Together with steps 2 and 5 for the raw categories and steps 6-8 for their finite-stage Karoubi envelopes, this proves all the claimed assertions.
